nodes.description: Frequent feeding prevents catabolic crises. GeneReviews recommends feeding neonates and infants every two to three hours. Suggested maximum fasting intervals when well are eight hours at 6–12 months, ten hours during the second year and twelve hours after age two. Illness, surgery and reduced intake require a more cautious individualized emergency plan, not a blanket twelve-hour allowance. Cornstarch or overnight feeding may be appropriate after infancy.

nodes.description: Common hypomorphic allele in several northern Indigenous populations. A patient fibroblast study found approximately 20% residual activity and partial resistance to malonyl-CoA inhibition. Most homozygotes are asymptomatic, but supervised fasting in five children demonstrated reduced ketogenesis and symptomatic hypoglycemia in two. Population associations with infectious illness and infant mortality do not establish a direct immune defect or an inevitable clinical outcome. In the Nunavik population-genetic study, the allele frequency was 95.5% among 100 analyzed adults after exclusions from 113 recruits; this is not disease prevalence or penetrance.
